title: Quashing of FIR - when High Courts actually intervene
p1:
An FIR can start a criminal case. But does it always have to continue?

Many people believe once an FIR is registered, the accused has no option until trial. That is not always true.
p2:
A High Court can step in and quash an FIR in specific situations, especially when continuing the case would be an abuse of the legal process.

For example, if the allegations do not disclose any actual offence, or the dispute is clearly a private matter being given a criminal colour, the court may intervene.
p3:
The surprising part: High Courts do not decide guilt or innocence at this stage. They only examine whether the case itself has a valid legal foundation.

The takeaway? An FIR is the beginning of an investigation, not automatic proof of wrongdoing. The law provides remedies when criminal proceedings are misused.
conclusion: Should courts have wider powers to stop criminal cases that appear to be filed only to harass someone? What is your view?
